title: What Grocery Budgeting Is and Why It Matters
summary: The foundations of grocery budgeting: what it is and why getting it right pays off.
body:
The average US household spends $400-$600/month on groceries. Meal planning, list discipline, and store-brand swaps cut 20-30% without eating worse.

title: Getting Started: Your First Five Moves in Grocery Budgeting
summary: Start grocery budgeting this week with five concrete moves.
body:
Don't try to do everything. Do these five, in order:

1. Inventory fridge/freezer/pantry
2. Plan 5-7 dinners around sales
3. Write the list by store section
4. Eat before shopping
5. Buy store brands first

Five moves, one week. Momentum beats perfection — the rest of this guide builds on exactly this start.
facts: Write the list by store section

title: Common Grocery Budgeting Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
summary: The mistakes everyone makes with grocery budgeting — and the fixes.
body:
The classic errors:

- Shopping hungry → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- No list → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Ignoring what's already at home → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.
- Buying bulk perishables that spoil → Fix: address it in your first week, not after it costs you.

Every mistake above is cheap to prevent and expensive to repair. Prevention is the whole game.

title: Grocery Budgeting Beginner FAQ
summary: Straight answers to the most common grocery budgeting questions.
body:
Q: How much should we spend?
A: USDA thrifty plan: ~$250/person/month; moderate ~$350.

Q: Coupons worth it?
A: Store apps + sales beat clipping for most.

Q: Bulk buying?
A: Only non-perishables you actually use.

Still stuck? Start with record 2 of this guide and do the first move today.
